author: review-agent
title: Full project review: tests C+, documentation C+, data not fit for training
body:
Principal review of the whole repository (journal #1).

- **Tests: C+.** Many tests passed without executing the solvers; data checks were mixed into the unit run; test runs polluted the audit ledger.
- **Documentation: C+.** Stale commands, the retired Markdown dataset layer still described, skills in mixed languages.
- **Data: NOT fit for training.** grounded-paraphrase injected unstated negative premises into about 64% of the training mix; about 70% of the mix came from one templated corpus; targets were predictable from the CONTEXT block instead of the message.

Consequence recorded then: no corpus qualified, and training stayed prohibited regardless (AGENTS.md rule 3). This review started the test hardening, the documentation fixes, the corpus-audit checker and, after the owner's language decisions, the full data rebuild.

Seeded on 2026-09-29 from the journal and reports; the timestamp is that of the source event.

author: test-agent
title: Test hardening: 508 tests pass and solver-backed tests really execute the solvers
body:

- Long data tests moved to a separate `npm run test:data`.

author: agent
title: Two agents paused for a session restart; annotations did not survive
body:
At 17:31Z the evaluation-tooling agent paused before any rebuild (corpora consistent, 545/545 tests green, a noise fix pending the next rebuild) and the data-expansion research agent paused with 150 pilot messages written and annotation pending (journal #58, #59).

After the restart (17:50Z, journal #61) **no annotations had survived**; the two independent annotator tracks were re-run over the 150 pilot messages. Lesson: work kept only in a scratchpad is lost on restart; results must be written to the repository before a pause.

Seeded on 2026-09-29 from the journal and reports; the timestamp is that of the source event.

author: project-history-agent
title: Sharding and git cleanup: one clean commit without files over 50 MB
body:
There is no journal event for this work; this note is reconstructed from the repository and says only what the files show.

- Commit `c55f23b` (2026-09-28 19:47 +02:00, "Sharded large data files, one model language, regenerated corpora") changed 615 files.
- `cleanGitCommit.sh` folds the unpushed local commits into one clean commit that contains no file larger than 50 MB (backup copy and backup branch first, `git reset --soft origin/main`, index rebuilt, size check, one commit, push after confirmation; `--rollback` restores).
- The commit added `datasets_sources/` to `.gitignore` (7 files under it remain tracked). `eval/reports/current/` was already gitignored, so the current reports exist only in the working tree.
- The size rule is in AGENTS.md "Key Paths": large JSONL is stored as `<name>.part-NNN.jsonl` shards through `lib/jsonl-shards.mjs`; `node tools/shard-large-files.mjs --check` and `tests/file-size-limit.test.mjs` enforce it.

Uncertain: who ran the script and with which flags is not recorded.

title: Owner: GPU shared that night with small inference models; single-worker rule suspended for that case
body:
Journal #86 (actor `owner-via-orchestrator`): the owner ran 0.5B/1.5B/1.7B inference-only models on the GPU in another session. The single-GPU-worker rule (AGENTS.md direction 2) was suspended for that combination for the night. Consequence: the shared unified memory later triggered the training container's CUDA-free floor several times (see training-experiments).

author: llm-jobs-agent
title: LLM batch work runs as LLMJobs job specs; tiers by configuration; proxy enforces budgets and tags (implemented)
body: Implementation of the owner decisions of 2026-10-02: (1) every LLM batch job is a declarative spec run by deterministic code (LLMJobs/, self-contained and reusable; ChatSOP's jobs, templates and plugins in jobs/); agents read only summary.md (<=10 lines) and escalations.jsonl. (2) Jobs name tiers or roles only: planner and decider good (deepseek-v4.1-flash), auditor medium (v4-flash), worker small (openference Qwen3.8 27b), worker-short tiny (local Qwen3-4B); concrete fallback chains in jobs/llmjobs.config.json until the proxy serves a tier. (3) Adaptive tiers: ladder per task kind, per-item climbing, start tier learned from the append-only state/llm-jobs/tier-stats.jsonl, periodic re-probe of a cheaper tier. (4) Work hygiene: every run writes only state/llm-jobs/<job>/<run-id>/; append-only index; published summaries go to dated run-named paths. (5) LLMAPIProvider refuses a registered run at its budget (402) and untagged or unknown-purpose requests beyond 100 per day (403). (6) Large inputs with instructions run as tasks: one planner call over templates, deterministic plan validation, execution, storage through the existing store path. Fixed shared summary.md writers found: tools/eval/kbqa/report.mjs, tools/eval/pragmatics/run.mjs, tools/eval/query-model-calibration/report.mjs, tools/linking/core-en/summary.mjs (and the cumulative books-eval/index.md); listed in TODO.md, not changed (not owned).

author: tinyagent-agent
title: TinyAgent phase 1: one server for all model work; library and CLI are its clients
body: Implements the owner's TinyAgent decisions of 2026-10-03 (with the same-day corrections). The earlier proxy and job runner are merged into TinyAgent/ (generic; knows nothing about SOP). One server per machine (tinyagent serve, 127.0.0.1:18080, same OpenAI/Anthropic API plus /v1/jobs, /v1/tasks, /v1/skills, /v1/run, /v1/ops, /v1/local) does providers and tiers, rate/plan limits and throttling, local model servers (slots, idle stop, exclusive groups), cache (use/strict/record; cut answers never cached), audit, costs, budgets, purposes. Clients (createTinyAgent; project access lib/tinyagent.mjs) auto-start it when none answers; the port bind decides between two starters; no cross-process locks. Home ~/.tinyagent (template config and key files written on first start; old key folder read as fallback; migrate-home copies old logs/cache/audit with verification). Layers: TinyAgent/config.default.json < ~/.tinyagent/config.json < config/tinyagent.json. Tiers: nano Qwen3-0.6B (official Qwen GGUF downloaded into models/), micro Qwen3-4B (supertiny alias), tiny MoE always on; without keys tiny serves small..best. Priority classes interactive/normal/background (background held within 70% of plan windows). Duration caps per tier entry. Skills: built-ins (chat, json, job, task, write-plugin), project SkillPlugins jobs/skills/, job folders, task templates; run = plan on good + deterministic execution; generated plugins run in a worker + vm sandbox with an allow-listed API (live check: a model-written plugin extracted and totalled 3 purchases into totals.csv). Every project model call goes through it (tests/no-direct-model-calls.test.mjs). Phase 2 after the ingestion-v2 agent commits: migrate its files, delete shims and legacy headers, switch 18080 to tinyagent serve.

author: tinyagent-agent
title: TinyAgent run: plan as code, visible plan cache, BM25 + tiny match (measured on 12 tasks)
body:
**What.** `tinyagent run "<instructions>" [--workdir DIR]` is a small coding-style agent with a visible plan cache (TODO §0 item, owner 2026-10-03). The planner tier (`good`) writes the plan as code: an .mjs module with `meta` (a typed parameter schema plus the example values), `run(tools, params)` and an optional `check`. It runs in the plugin sandbox, with the tools confined to the work folder: read, list, search, write, move, ask, runSkillScript. A plan that passed its check is stored `verified` in `<workdir>/.tinyagent/plans/<id>/` (plan.mjs, PLAN.md, runs.jsonl). Before planning, BM25 over the cached plans finds candidates and `tiny` decides "same task, other parameters"; the values are type-checked against the schema and must occur in the request. A hit runs the cached plan with no planner call. A plan edited by hand changes its hash, and its check re-verifies it before it is reused.

**Measured once** (`TinyAgent/bench/agent-tasks.mjs`, 12 tasks with known results; reports in `eval/reports/current/tinyagent-agent/2026-10-03-r1`, `-r2`, `-r3-skill`):
- r1: 10 of 12 correct. Variants: 5 of 5 reused, 4 correct. The fifth reused a plan that had hard-coded `.txt`; tiny noticed the difference in its reason but still matched. One near miss failed to plan in 3 rounds: the planner never saw the file and parsed a prose line as the table header.
- Generic fixes after r1:
  - A deterministic refusal of plans that write a request value into their code.
  - The first lines of the files the request names, and of the files a failed plan read, go to the planner.
  - A skill's body is given when the plan uses that skill.
  - The match prompt now says that every differing detail must be a parameter.
- r2: 12 of 12 correct. 4 of 5 variants reused, all 4 correct; 0 of 3 near misses reused. Of 8 new plans, 3 were right at the first round and 5 after a re-plan. Two of those re-plans came from a skill name wrongly flagged as a hard-coded value; that is fixed, and in r3 the skill variant is reused.
- Latency:
  - Cache hit: one local `tiny` call and 0 credits. 1.7 to 8 s; the median was 3.7 s in r1 and 8.2 s in r2, while the local model was shared.
  - New plan: 3 to 4 calls, 0.75 to 3 credits, 8 to 80 s.
  - BM25 itself takes well under 1 ms.

**Stopped** at that point, because the answer is clear: reuse works with high precision and saves the planner entirely. The weak point is the first-plan success of new tasks (planner bugs, and checks that re-implement definitions); a prompt rule for checks was added after r3 and has not been measured.

author: tasklambda-agent
title: TaskLambdas and TaskLambdaCalls: concept model, call folders, reuse rules, bench after the rename
body: Concept: a TaskLambda is code + typed params + optional check + origin + a required effects declaration; Agent Skills are instructions a TaskLambda may use. A TaskLambdaCall is one invocation with a folder (call.json, output.json, effects.jsonl, inputs.jsonl, models.jsonl, log.txt, summary.json, child calls nested), so the folders form an auditable cache of past activity; nested calls record parent and root. Decision: job runs and task folders are wrapped by their calls (linked), not moved; a job run has one child call per item (packed calls listed with shared). Reuse: only pure TaskLambdas, by hash+params+workdir+attachments, and only while every recorded input (file read, listing, search) has the same hash; effectful calls always run. Prune keeps call.json, output.json, summary.json after 30 days. Bench (12 tasks, planner good, match tiny): 11/12; the miss exposed a gap in the hard-coded value check (one-character literals), fixed generically (a one-digit literal the request holds).
